result.note: Tests the functions of the new Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority and how it relates to the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, the Union Cabinet approved an Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA). Consider the following statements about it:
items: It will prepare a national transport master plan covering a horizon of at least five years.
It will technically appraise central government infrastructure projects costing INR 5 billion or more.
It will assess the impact of major projects after their completion.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the master plan will cover at least ten years. Five-year and annual plans are the ministries' own plans, which ITLA will assess against that framework. The plan spans roads, railways, ports, aviation, waterways, urban mobility and logistics.
questions.source: ITLA will technically appraise central government infrastructure projects costing INR 5 billion (USD 51.9 million) or more.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Prime Minister Gati Shakti National Master Plan, as of 2026:
items: Approval and delivery of projects remain with individual ministries and states.
By August 2026, its Network Planning Group had evaluated 198 projects in all.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the Network Planning Group had evaluated 396 projects, of which 198 were under implementation. Gati Shakti brings ministries and states onto a shared digital planning platform, and the new ITLA is meant to complement that framework.
questions.source: By August, its Network Planning Group had evaluated 396 projects, with 198 under implementation.
